speaker: A
text: Air pollution causes around 40,000 early deaths a year in the UK.

speaker: A
text: Road traffic is the biggest single source of air pollution in UK cities.

speaker: A
text: Ghent council's report says footfall in Ghent's centre went up after cars were restricted in 2017.

speaker: B
text: The 40,000 figure is a modelled estimate from 2016, not a count of actual deaths.

speaker: B
text: Banning cars from city centres would devastate small businesses that rely on deliveries and passing trade.

speaker: B
text: Nearly 70 percent of shoppers on UK high streets arrive by car.

speaker: A
text: Small businesses would benefit from banning cars from city centres.

speaker: A
text: Pedestrians spend more per month in local shops than drivers do.

speaker: A
text: London's ultra low emission zone cut roadside nitrogen dioxide by nearly half in central London.

speaker: B
text: People should be free to choose how they travel.

speaker: B
text: Public transport in most UK cities is too unreliable to replace the car.

speaker: A
text: Government figures show bus use outside London has fallen by a third since 2010.

speaker: A
text: The answer is to invest in buses rather than keep cars in city centres.

speaker: B
text: Electric cars will make the pollution argument irrelevant within ten years.
